home.description: Kroky is an iPhone app that notices when you've been sitting, waits for dry weather and plans a walking loop from where you are, just long enough to close the gap to today's step goal.
home.eyebrow: Walk breaks for desk workers · iPhone
home.h1: You've sat two hours. It's dry until 5:50 PM. Here's a 25-minute walk.
home.lead: Kroky notices when you've been sitting, waits for dry weather and plans a loop from where you are, sized to close the gap to today's step goal. Tap Go and it guides you, every turn.
home.facts: Free to start · No account · iPhone, iOS 17 or later
how.1: Kroky reads your steps from Apple Health. After a long stretch without steps (90 minutes unless you change it), it's time for a walk.
how.2: It checks the hourly forecast and finds today's dry window, so the walk doesn't start in the rain.
how.3_t: It plans a loop sized to your gap
how.3: From where you are and back, long enough to close the gap to today's step goal, or 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes. It goes through parks and quiet streets where it can, and comes back a different way when the streets allow.
how.4: Kroky guides you on a live map, with spoken directions if you like, even with the screen locked. Apple Maps or Google Maps are one tap away if you prefer them.
features.1: A notification after a long sit, only in the hours and on the days you choose, at most twice a day, and only when it's dry out.
features.2: Home shows how long it stays dry, from Apple Weather's hourly forecast. Kroky can remind you when a dry window opens.
features.3_t: A loop that closes the gap
features.3: Steps turn into distance with your own stride, learned from your walks. The loop is just long enough for the steps you have left today.
features.4: Follow the loop on a live map with the walked part greyed out, distance and time left, and optional spoken directions.
features.5: Shuffle for a different loop, reverse it, rate it, keep the ones you like and mark a street to avoid. Kroky won't offer the same new loop twice in a week.
features.6: Walks this week, steps added, a streak, each walk's result and your walk history with every route.
features.7: With your permission, Kroky checks your calendar on your iPhone and stays quiet while you're busy.
features.8: Distances follow your iPhone's region settings. Kroky speaks 49 languages.
privacy.1: Your steps, settings and walk history stay on the device. There is no Kroky server.
privacy.2: Open the app and set a goal. There is nothing to sign up for.
privacy.3: No analytics, no ads, no tracking SDKs. Location is used while Kroky is open, and during a walk you start, until you end it.

faq.1_a: Kroky: Walk Breaks is an iPhone app for people who sit a lot. It notices when you've been sitting, checks when it's dry outside and plans a walking loop from where you are, sized to close the gap to today's step goal. Then it guides you around the loop on a live map.
faq.2_q: Is there an app that reminds me to take a walk when I've been sitting too long?
faq.2_a: Yes. Kroky reads your steps from Apple Health and, after a long stretch without steps, sends a nudge with a walk ready to go. You choose the hours, the days and how long a sit counts as too long; the default is 90 minutes, from 9 AM to 6 PM on weekdays. It sends at most two nudges a day and only when it's dry. Sitting nudges are part of Kroky Pro.
faq.3_q: Which app plans a walking route to reach my daily step goal?
faq.3_a: Kroky does. It takes the steps you still need today, turns them into a distance with your own stride, and plans a loop that starts and ends where you are and is just that long. You can also pick a 15, 30, 45 or 60-minute walk instead.
faq.4_q: Can Kroky find a walking loop near me that avoids main roads?
faq.4_a: It tries to. Kroky looks for parks and footpaths around you with Apple Maps and OpenStreetMap, plans the loop through them and keeps off busy streets where the map allows. If you don't like a stretch, mark it and future loops will avoid it.
faq.5_q: Does Kroky check the weather before suggesting a walk?
faq.5_a: Yes. It uses Apple Weather's hourly forecast to find today's dry window and shows how long it stays dry. Nudges only come when it's dry, and Kroky Pro can remind you when a dry window opens.
faq.6_a: Kroky is free to download and use, with one new loop and one shuffle a day, today's dry window, your steps, live guidance, your weekly view and walk history. Kroky Pro adds sitting nudges, weather reminders, Skip my meetings, unlimited loops and shuffles, and your favorite loops mixed back in. It's a yearly subscription with a 7-day free trial, or a one-time lifetime purchase.
faq.7_a: No. There is no sign-up and no login. Open the app, allow Apple Health access and set a daily goal of 6,000, 8,000 or 10,000 steps.
faq.8_a: Only when you ask it to. Kroky uses your location while the app is open, to plan a loop and get the weather, and continuously only during a walk you start, from Go until you end it. It never asks for "Always" location and never tracks you outside a walk. Your routes stay on your iPhone.
faq.9_q: Does it work with Apple Watch?
faq.9_a: Kroky has no Apple Watch app, but it reads your steps from Apple Health, which counts the steps from your iPhone and your Apple Watch together. So a walk with your watch on counts toward your goal.
faq.10_q: Does Kroky guide me during the walk?
faq.10_a: Yes. Tap Go and Kroky shows where you are on the loop, the part you've walked, and the distance and time left. Spoken directions are optional, and guidance keeps working with the screen locked. You can also open the loop in Apple Maps or Google Maps.
faq.11_q: Is Kroky on Android or iPad?
faq.11_a: Not yet. Kroky is for iPhone, with iOS 17 or later.
faq.12_a: Anywhere Apple Maps has walking directions. Loops are best where there are parks and footpaths nearby; in places with few, Kroky plans the quietest loop it can, or a walk there and back.
faq.13_a: 49: English, Arabic, Bengali, Catalan, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French (France and Canada), German, Greek, Gujarati, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Korean, Malay, Malayalam, Marathi, Norwegian, Odia, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu and Vietnamese, with British and Australian English.
faq.14_q: What does the name Kroky mean?
faq.14_a: "Steps." It's the Ukrainian word кроки written in Latin letters, and the Czech and Slovak word as it is.
faq.15_a: nakolini, a two-person studio of engineers Dmytro Hryb and Vitalii Kikot, who build apps and put AI to work for companies. See nakolini.com.

g1.title: An app that reminds you to walk when you've sat too long · Kroky
g1.description: Kroky for iPhone notices when you've been sitting, waits for dry weather and nudges you with a walk sized to your step goal. How it works, and how to set it up.
g1.h1: An app that reminds you to walk when you've sat too long
g1.answer: Kroky is an iPhone app that reads your steps from Apple Health, notices a long stretch without them and, when it's dry outside, nudges you with a walk that's ready to go: a loop from where you are, sized to close the gap to today's step goal.
g1.why_h2: Why a step-based reminder works better than a timer
g1.why: A timer nudges you every hour whether or not you've moved. Kroky counts real steps, so a walk to a meeting or the kitchen resets the clock, and a nudge only comes when you've really been still. It also waits for a dry window and stays inside the hours you set, so a reminder is a walk you can take now, not one more alert to dismiss.
g1.setup_1: Allow Kroky to read steps from Apple Health. It only reads; it never writes.
g1.setup_2: Pick a daily goal: 6,000, 8,000 or 10,000 steps.
g1.setup_3: Set the hours and days Kroky may nudge you, for example 9 AM to 6 PM on weekdays.
g1.setup_4: In Settings, choose how long a sit counts as too long (90 minutes to start), and turn on Skip my meetings if you want quiet during calendar events.
g1.limits: Sitting nudges are part of Kroky Pro; the free plan gives you a new loop every day when you open the app. Kroky sends at most two nudges a day. iOS decides exactly when an app can check in the background, so a nudge can come a little later than expected.
g2.title: How long do I need to walk to reach my step goal? · Kroky
g2.description: At an easy pace, 1,000 steps take about 10 minutes and cover about 750 m (0.5 mi). A table of steps to minutes and distance, and how Kroky sizes a walk to your gap.
g2.h1: How long do I need to walk to reach my step goal?
g2.answer: At an easy walking pace of about 100 steps a minute, 1,000 steps take about 10 minutes and cover about 750 m (0.5 mi). So 3,000 steps left is a walk of about 30 minutes and 2.2 km (1.4 mi).
g2.table_note: With a stride of 0.75 m and a pace of 80 m a minute. Taller people and faster walkers cover more ground per step and per minute.
g2.own: Stride and pace differ from person to person. Kroky starts from your walking step length in Apple Health and, after two walks with Kroky, uses the stride and pace from your own walks, so the steps it plans match the steps Health counts.
g2.kroky: Home shows the steps you have left today. Tap Close gap and Kroky plans a loop from where you are that's just long enough, or pick 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes.
g3.title: How to find a walking loop near you that starts and ends at your door · Kroky
g3.description: Kroky plans a walking loop from where you are, through parks and quiet streets, back a different way, at the length you need. How it finds the route and what you can change.
g3.h1: How to find a walking loop near you that starts and ends at your door
g3.answer: Open Kroky and tap Walk Now: it plans a loop that starts and ends where you are, goes through nearby parks and quiet streets where it can, comes back a different way when the streets allow, and is as long as the steps or minutes you want.
g3.how: Kroky looks for parks, footpaths and main roads around you with Apple Maps and OpenStreetMap, picks a few points through the green and asks Apple Maps for walking directions between them. It tries several shapes and keeps the one closest to the length you need, with the least time beside busy roads.
g3.change_2: Reverse it to walk the other way round.
g3.change_3: Avoid part of a walk you didn't like; future loops keep off it.
g3.change_4: Keep a loop you liked, and Kroky Pro mixes your favorites back in.
g3.limits: Loops come from map data, so check what's in front of you: paths can be closed, unlit or muddy. Where there are few parks or paths, Kroky plans the quietest loop it can, or a walk there and back.
support.title: Kroky Support
support.description: Help with Kroky: Walk Breaks. Steps from Apple Health, nudges, restoring and cancelling Kroky Pro, avoided places, and how to contact us.
support.steps_q: Why doesn't Kroky show my steps?
support.steps_a:
Kroky reads steps from Apple Health. If Home says "Kroky can't see your steps", it assumes you've been sitting.

To turn access on, open the Health app, tap your profile picture, then Apps under Privacy. Choose Kroky and turn on Steps and Walking Step Length. Also check that Settings › Privacy & Security › Motion & Fitness › Fitness Tracking is on, so your iPhone counts steps at all.
support.nudges_q: Why am I not getting nudges?
support.nudges_a:
Check these, in order:

Kroky Pro. Sitting nudges and weather reminders are part of Kroky Pro.
Nudges are on. In Kroky, open Settings (the gear on Home) and check that "Nudges and weather reminders" is on, and how long you have to sit before one comes.
Nudge hours and days. Kroky only nudges between the hours and on the days set under "Nudge me between". With Skip my meetings on, it also stays quiet when your calendar shows you as busy.
Notifications. In the iOS Settings app › Notifications › Kroky, allow notifications.

Kroky sends at most 2 nudges a day. iOS decides exactly when the app can check in the background, so a nudge can come a little later than expected, and opening Kroky now and then helps.
support.loop_q: Why can't Kroky plan a loop here?
support.loop_a: Kroky needs your location and a connection to plan a loop. If it says "Couldn't build a loop of this length here", try a shorter or longer walk, or Shuffle. In places with few streets or paths, it may offer a walk there and back instead.
support.restore_q: How do I restore Kroky Pro on a new iPhone?
support.restore_a: Sign in with the Apple Account that bought Kroky Pro. Then, in Kroky, open Settings (the gear on Home) and tap Restore Purchases in the Kroky Pro section. The Restore Purchases link on the Kroky Pro screen does the same. This works for both the yearly plan and the lifetime unlock.
support.cancel_q: How do I cancel the yearly subscription?
support.cancel_a:
In Kroky, open Settings › Manage Subscription. Or, in the iOS Settings app, tap your name › Subscriptions › Kroky. Cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date and you won't be charged again. Kroky Pro stays on until the end of the period you paid for, or until the free trial ends. Apple handles all billing and refunds, so for a refund go to reportaproblem.apple.com.

The lifetime unlock is a single payment, not a subscription, so there's nothing to cancel.
support.avoid_q: How do I remove an avoided place?
support.avoid_a: In Kroky, open Settings › Avoided places. Swipe left on a place and tap Remove, or tap Clear All to remove every one. Future loops may use those streets again.
support.data_a: It stays on your iPhone. Kroky has no account and no server. See the Privacy Policy for what goes to Apple and OpenStreetMap to plan loops and check the weather.
support.contact_tip: Please include your iPhone model, your iOS version and a short description of what happened. A screenshot or screen recording helps a lot. You can write in any language.

privacy_page.title: Kroky Privacy Policy
privacy_page.description: Kroky: Walk Breaks collects nothing: no account, no server, no analytics. What the app uses on your iPhone, and what goes to Apple and OpenStreetMap to plan walks and check the weather.
privacy_page.intro: Kroky: Walk Breaks ("Kroky") is an iPhone app that suggests walks. This policy explains, in plain language, what the app uses, where it goes and what stays on your iPhone. The short version: we don't collect anything. Kroky has no server, no account and no analytics. The few things that leave your iPhone go to Apple or to OpenStreetMap so the app can find parks, plan a route and check the weather.
privacy_page.who: Kroky is made by nakolini, a studio of Dmytro Hryb and Vitalii Kikot ("we"). You can reach us at {email}.
privacy_page.collect: Nothing. We don't receive your steps, your location, your calendar or anything else. There is no login and no server we run. If you email us, we receive your email and use it only to answer you.
privacy_page.health: Kroky reads your step count, and your walking step length to turn steps into distance, from Apple Health, to know when you've been sitting and how many steps are left today. It only reads Health data; it never writes to Health. Your Health data is read and used on your iPhone and is never sent anywhere, unless you export your walks from a test version yourself (see below). It is never used for advertising or shared with anyone.
privacy_page.location_1: Kroky asks for location only while you're using the app, never "Always". It gets one location fix when you plan a walk and when Home shows the weather, to plan a loop near you and to get the weather forecast.
privacy_page.location_2: During a walk you start, Kroky follows your location to show where you are on the route, including while the screen is locked; iOS shows the location indicator while it does. It stops when the walk ends. The route you walked is kept only on your iPhone, in your walk history, until you delete that walk. Kroky never tracks you outside a walk you started.
privacy_page.location_3: Kroky saves the last location on your iPhone, rounded to two decimal places (about 1 km), so it can check the weather for walk reminders without asking for your location again.
privacy_page.location_4: Test versions of Kroky (TestFlight) can export the walk history as a file, to help improve the app. The file holds each walk's precise route and times, its step counts from Apple Health (including how many came from your iPhone and how many from your Apple Watch), the app version and time zone it was walked with, whether Precise Location was on, and the voice settings and spoken directions used on the walk. It names no one: the only device details are the iPhone model and iOS version. It is made on your iPhone and leaves it only if you choose to share it. The App Store version has no export.
privacy_page.leaves_h2: What leaves your iPhone, and to whom
privacy_page.leaves_weather: Apple Weather (WeatherKit) receives a location (your current one on Home, or the rounded saved one for reminders) to return the hourly forecast. This goes through Apple and is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.
privacy_page.leaves_maps: Apple Maps (MapKit) receives the start and turning points of your walk to plan walking routes, and the area around you to find parks the walk goes through. During a walk, it also receives your current location when Kroky plans the way to the start, back to the route or home. This goes through Apple.
privacy_page.leaves_osm: OpenStreetMap's Overpass API (overpass-api.de, or the public mirror overpass.private.coffee when it's busy) receives the area to search for parks, main roads and footpaths, so loops can keep off busy streets: an approximate starting point, rounded to about 100 m, and a search radius. No account, device identifier or other personal data is sent with it. The results are cached on your iPhone for a month (and used for up to six months if Overpass can't be reached), so the same area isn't asked for again.
privacy_page.leaves_handoff: Google Maps or Apple Maps receives the loop only if you choose Open in Google Maps or Open in Apple Maps; Go follows the walk in Kroky itself. That app's own privacy policy applies from then on.
privacy_page.calendar: Only if you turn on Skip my meetings, Kroky reads your calendar on your iPhone to find the times you're busy, so it doesn't nudge you during meetings. It uses only the start and end times and whether you're marked busy. Your calendar is never sent anywhere.
privacy_page.notifications: Walk nudges are local notifications scheduled on your iPhone. Kroky doesn't use a push server.
privacy_page.purchases: Kroky Pro is sold as a yearly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase, both handled by Apple's App Store. Apple handles your payment details and billing, and they never reach us. The app only sees your entitlement: which plan you have and, for the subscription, when it renews or ends. Kroky checks it with Apple and remembers it on your iPhone.
privacy_page.stays_h2: What stays on your iPhone, and for how long
privacy_page.stays: Your settings, step goal, nudge hours, the loops you were offered and how you rated them, your walks, the places you asked Kroky to avoid and the cached map data are stored only on your iPhone. They stay until you delete them in the app or delete the app, which deletes them all. They are included in your iPhone's own backups, which Apple handles.
privacy_page.choices: Every permission can be changed at any time: Health access in the Health app (your profile › Apps › Kroky), location, notifications and calendar in the iOS Settings app › Kroky. Kroky keeps working without each of them, with less to offer. Because we hold no data about you, there is nothing for us to show, correct or delete; the data on your iPhone is yours to delete. If you have a question about your rights under data protection law, such as the GDPR, write to us.
privacy_page.tracking: Kroky has no analytics, advertising, crash-reporting or tracking SDKs, no account system and no third-party code beyond Apple's own frameworks. We don't track you across apps or websites, and we don't sell or share any data.
privacy_page.website: This website has no cookies, no analytics and no tracking. It is hosted on GitHub Pages, which may keep technical logs such as IP addresses to keep the service secure; see GitHub's Privacy Statement.
privacy_page.children: Kroky isn't directed at children under 13, and it doesn't collect personal information from anyone.
privacy_page.changes: If this policy changes, the new version will appear at this address with a new effective date.

terms_page.intro: These terms apply to Kroky: Walk Breaks ("Kroky"), an iPhone app made by nakolini, a studio of Dmytro Hryb and Vitalii Kikot ("we"). By downloading or using Kroky, you agree to them. If you don't agree, please don't use the app.
terms_page.license: Kroky is licensed to you, not sold, under Apple's Licensed Application End User License Agreement (the standard EULA). These terms add what's specific to Kroky. If they conflict, the standard EULA applies.
terms_page.safety_1: Kroky plans routes automatically from Apple Maps and OpenStreetMap data. That data can be out of date or wrong: a path can be closed, private, unlit, muddy, steep or cross a busy road without a crossing. You decide where and when it's safe to walk. Follow traffic rules and local signs, keep your eyes on your surroundings rather than the screen, and don't walk where you don't feel safe.
terms_page.safety_2: Weather forecasts come from Apple Weather and can be wrong. Dress for the weather you see, not only the one forecast.
terms_page.health: Kroky is a general wellness app. It is not a medical device and gives no medical advice. Step counts, distances and times are estimates. If you have a health condition, are pregnant or haven't been active for a while, talk to a doctor before you start walking more.
terms_page.pro_1: Kroky is free to use. Kroky Pro adds features and is sold through the App Store as a yearly subscription with a 7-day free trial, or as a one-time lifetime purchase. The price for your country is shown in the app before you buy.
terms_page.pro_2: Payment is charged to your Apple Account when you confirm the purchase, or when the free trial ends. The yearly subscription renews automatically unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the current period; your Apple Account is charged for the renewal within the 24 hours before the period ends. terms_page.use: Use Kroky for your own personal walks. Don't reverse-engineer, decompile or resell it, or use it for anything unlawful.

terms_page.warranty: We work hard to make Kroky useful and reliable, but it is provided "as is". We can't promise that a loop, a forecast or a step count is always right, or that the app will always be available.
terms_page.liability: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential damages, or for injury, loss or damage that comes from following a route or a forecast. Nothing in these terms limits liability that can't be limited by law, or your rights as a consumer in your country.
